questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
To improve their economic performance, Eastern European countries have switched from planned economies to mixed economies. What is likely to be the most common outcome of such a change?

options.A: short-term and long-term success in improving economic performance
options.B: short-term and long-term failure in improving economic performance
options.C: short-term failure and long-term success in improving economic performance
options.D: short-term success and long-term failure in improving economic performance

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the change in a country’s production possibility curve from PQ to PR. P public goods O Q R private goods What increases as a result of the change from PQ to PR?

options.C: the opportunity cost of private goods
options.D: the opportunity cost of public goods

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a production possibility curve for an economy. X consumer goods Y O capital goods Assuming that the production possibility curve remains unchanged, what is the most likely reason for the movement from point X to point Y?

options.A: a civil war causing a widespread loss of resources
options.B: a permanent fall in productivity in both capital and consumer goods
options.C: the exhaustion of a natural resource
options.D: the rise in unemployment due to a recession

questions.questionText: Buses currently run every two hours between X and Y. The bus company which operates the service decides to introduce an hourly service. How will this most likely affect the number of passengers carried per day and the number of passengers carried per journey? number of number of passengers per day passengers per journey

The table refers to exports of sugar from Jamaica in 1999 and 2000. exports of sugar export earnings (tonnes) from sugar (US$ millions) 1999 177522 95.79 2000 180481 83.8 What can be concluded from the data?

options.A: The demand for sugar was price elastic.
options.B: The income elasticity of demand for sugar was negative.
options.C: The price of sugar in US$ fell between 1999 and 2000.
options.D: The supply of sugar was price elastic.

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of demand for grapes is –2.0. When the price is $15, quantity demanded is 5000 units. How much will be demanded when the price falls to $12?

The Toyota Motor Corporation makes cars in response to customer orders rather than attempting to sell cars it has already built. If the company received a large increase in orders for its Prius model, what will be expected of its current supply curve on a demand and supply diagram?

options.C: It will shift to the left.
options.D: It will shift to the right.

questions.questionText: The table shows the demand and supply schedules for a good before and after the imposition of a tax. price quantity quantity supplied quantity supplied ($) demanded before tax after tax
340 230 0 What was the amount of the tax?
What is the likely nature of the price elasticity of supply of a crop such as rice?

options.A: highly elastic in both the short and the long run as rice is an essential product
options.B: highly elastic in the short run and more inelastic in the long run as production methods improve
options.C: highly inelastic in both the short and the long run as the land area of a country is fixed
options.D: highly inelastic in the short run and more elastic in the long run as it takes time to plant rice

questions.questionText: During a certain period, 10000 units of a normal good are sold at a price of US$20. During a later period, 12000 units are sold at a price of US$22. What could explain this change?

options.B: an increase in the cost of raw materials
options.C: an increase in the price of a substitute commodity
options.D: an increase in the productivity of factors of production

questions.questionText: The final of a major sports event is held in a stadium which has a fixed capacity of 40000 people. The price for a seat is set at P but when the tickets go on sale all tickets are sold very quickly F with many disappointed people unable to buy a ticket. Which diagram best represents this?

options.A: B S S P F price price P F
options.D: F D O O 40 000 40 000 quantity quantity
options.C: D S S P F price price P

questions.questionText: In recent years, downloading music to computers and other electronic devices has become more popular replacing other ways of buying music, e.g. compact discs (CDs). What is likely to happen to the price and the amount of resources allocated to each of these markets? downloaded music market CD market resources resources price price allocated allocated

The table shows how much rice and wheat two countries, X and Y, can grow when each country divides its resources equally between growing rice and wheat. country X country Y rice (units) 900million 100million wheat (units) 300million 50million Assume that each country now specialises according to comparative advantage and trades with the other country. Which terms of trade would benefit both countries?

The table gives details of the balance of trade in the US in 2011 and 2012. 2011 2012 value of goods exported (US$ millions) 1496000 1561000 value of goods imported (US$ millions) 2240000 2303000 balance of trade in goods (US$ millions) –744000 –742000 balance of trade in goods and services (US$ millions) –557000 –535000 What can be concluded about the US in 2012?

options.A: The balance of trade in goods worsened.
options.B: The balance of trade in services improved.
options.C: The prices of goods imported and exported increased.
options.D: The volumes of goods imported and exported increased.

questions.questionText: A country increases its labour productivity in the manufacturing industry. What is least likely to result from this?

options.B: higher levels of exports of manufacturing

What will be the impact on demand-pull inflation and on cost-push inflation of an increase in indirect taxes? demand-pull cost-push inflation inflation

At the start of 2009, a worker earned US$100 a week. In 2009, the Retail Price Index (RPI) rose by 4% and his average wage rose by 7%. In 2010, the RPI fell by 3% and his wage fell by 2%. What happened to his real wage between the start of 2009 and the end of 2010?
A government has low reserves of foreign currency. When would it be most likely to consider a deficit on current account to be a serious problem?

options.A: when the country is experiencing a period of high, sustained growth
options.B: when the deficit alternates regularly with a surplus
options.C: when the deficit exceeds the sum of errors and omissions in the balance of payments account
options.D: when the level of international confidence in the country is low

The graph shows the movement of the £ sterling against the US$ over a three-month period in 2013. £1 = US$1.6 price of £ (US$) £1 = US$1.48 July 2013 Sept 2013 What could explain this change?

options.A: an increase in confidence about the UK economy
options.B: an increase in productivity in the US
options.C: an increase in UK Government debt
options.D: an increase in US interest rates

questions.questionText: China had US$155 billion current account surplus in 2012. Which combination of policies might the Chinese Government use to restore equilibrium?

options.A: Decrease income tax and raise the value of the Chinese currency, the Yuan.
options.B: Increase income tax and lower the value of the Chinese currency, the Yuan.
options.C: Increase subsidies to Chinese firms and reduce income tax.
